items.criterion: The recap runtime is between 111.0 seconds and 123.0 seconds inclusive (approximately one minute fifty-one seconds to two minutes three seconds).
items.why: Brief specifies a teaser running "just under two minutes." Window is the golden reference's 116.94 s ±5%; outside this band fails the deliverable as a trailer-length artefact.
items.check: Read the container duration; pass if 111.0 ≤ duration_s ≤ 123.0.

items.criterion: The recap is landscape 16:9, with the display aspect ratio ≥ 1.70 and ≤ 1.85, and width > height.
items.why: Brief specifies landscape 16:9.
items.check: Read display aspect ratio from the video stream; pass if width > height and DAR ∈ [1.70, 1.85].

items.criterion: The deliverable is an MP4 container with an H.264 video stream and an AAC audio stream.
items.why: Brief specifies MP4 / H.264 / AAC.
items.check: Read container format, video codec, audio codec; pass if format includes mp4 AND video codec is h264 AND audio codec is aac.

items.criterion: The recap does not display any channel-branding watermark, end-card, or persistent on-screen graphic naming "Earthling Cinema", "Wisecrack", "SUBSCRIBE", "LIKE", "FOLLOW", or thumbnails for other YouTube videos.
items.why: Brief explicitly forbids channel watermarks and subscription CTAs. The Earthling Cinema source ends with such an outro card.
items.check: Inspect the recap end-to-end for any of the listed brand strings or YouTube-style subscribe / thumbnail UI. Pass if none appear. Judge cites the recap timestamp of any such element if found.

items.criterion: The recap contains at least one clearly identifiable medium or close shot of an adult male with long unkempt dark hair, often in a dark leather coat or jacket and sometimes sunglasses, framed as the protagonist.
items.why: Source calibration: this is Oh Dae-su / Choi Min-sik, the protagonist; appearance is consistent across the embedded film clips (e.g. drunk police-station, sushi bar around 00:56–01:03, hallway fight around 03:16–03:21, lone-descent street scenes).
items.check: Judge cites at least one recap timestamp showing a man matching this description in a recognizable protagonist framing (close or medium, lit, face visible).

items.criterion: The recap contains at least one shot of an interior room that reads as a confined cell, small framed bed/chair/table, wallpapered or padded walls, no clear exit visible, with a single human inhabitant.
items.why: Source calibration: the hotel-room cell appears around 00:42–00:52 and 03:01–03:03 in the source. This is the inciting-mystery beat of the trailer.
items.check: Judge cites a recap timestamp showing an interior that visually reads as confinement (single occupant, no door context, claustrophobic framing).

items.criterion: The recap contains at least one outdoor shot in which the protagonist (long-haired adult male as identified in V-PROTAG-FACE) is alone in a public space in daylight or natural light, framed as if just released or first venturing out.
items.why: Source calibration: the release-from-suitcase beat at 00:17–00:19 / 00:54–00:55 and lone city-street descents (e.g. 04:15–04:18) carry this convention.
items.check: Judge cites a recap timestamp showing an exterior, natural-light shot with the protagonist alone or visually isolated in a public space.

items.criterion: The recap contains at least one shot of a different, well-dressed adult male character (suit or sharp shirt, neat hair, controlled posture) clearly distinct from the protagonist, framed as a threatening or controlling figure (e.g. interior with strong design, low-angle, or held gaze), and that shot is held on screen for at least 1.5 continuous seconds.
items.why: Source calibration: Lee Woo-jin in his penthouse and corridor moments, the antagonist's first reveal. Available non-spoiler at 01:09–01:14 and 02:39–02:48. The brief specifies he must be "seen once and held just long enough to register as the threat," so a flash insert does not satisfy the criterion.
items.check: Judge cites a recap timestamp range showing a well-dressed adult male, visually distinct from V-PROTAG-FACE, in a framing that reads as antagonist (controlled, observing, or threatening), and confirms the shot is held for >= 1.5 seconds continuous. The framing must not depict any confrontation that explains his motive in dialogue.

items.criterion: The recap contains at least one shot from a narrow corridor / hallway / tunnel-like green or steel-toned interior in which the protagonist is engaged with multiple visible attackers (three or more bodies in frame), with a weapon (hammer) or close-contact combat posture visible.
items.why: Source calibration: the canonical sideways-tracking one-shot corridor fight appears in the source only at 03:16–03:21 (~5 s). This is the curator-named iconic-action requirement and is the trailer's action-signature.
items.check: Judge cites a recap timestamp showing a narrow-corridor combat composition with three or more bodies and a weapon or close-contact stance. Duration ≥ 0.5 s of continuous corridor combat suffices.

items.criterion: The recap contains at least one close or medium shot of the protagonist with visible blood on his face or head and an aggressive, defiant, or hardened facial expression (not crying, not collapsed).
items.why: Source calibration: bloodied close-ups around 01:18–01:28, 03:38–03:40, 04:23–04:26 in the source. This is the trailer's "stakes" beat.
items.check: Judge cites a recap timestamp where a bloodied face matching V-PROTAG-FACE is in close or medium with a defiant / hard expression.

items.criterion: The first frame on which the "OLDBOY" / "OLD BOY" / "PARK CHAN-WOOK'S OLDBOY" title text becomes readable is positioned in the final 25% of the recap's runtime.
items.why: Trailer convention rewarded by the golden: title is the closing payoff, not a header. Golden lands at 01:47 of a 1:57 trailer (≈93% mark).
items.check: Compute recap_duration_s × 0.75. Find the first recap timestamp at which the title text appears; pass if that timestamp ≥ recap_duration_s × 0.75. Judge cites the timestamp.

items.criterion: The recap does not contain any frame showing the stylized "EARTHLING CINEMA" yellow halftone title card, the red velvet curtain backdrop with a glass dome on a plinth holding a small object (e.g. a Blu-ray case), or the framed "Wisecrack EARTHLING CINEMA SUBSCRIBE" end card.
items.why: The source's branding graphics (intro and outro) and host-stage set are the most visually distinctive elements in the source; including any of these signals total source-contamination. Note this item is about the GRAPHICS/SET; the host's FACE is covered by penalty item N-CRIT-HOST-VIDEO.
items.check: Inspect the recap end-to-end. Pass if no frame shows any of the listed graphics: yellow-halftone "Earthling Cinema" title text, red velvet stage backdrop with glass dome / plinth, or "Wisecrack / Earthling Cinema / SUBSCRIBE" composite end card. Judge cites the timestamp of any offending frame if found.

items.criterion: No persistent on-screen overlay element, for example a sports-style scoreboard widget, a lower-third caption/citation block, a numbered or named chapter title card sequence, a persistent attribution panel, or any other framing graphic that is not a burned-in subtitle and not a final title card, remains visible across more than 50% of the recap's total runtime.
items.why: Required by diversity constraint `output_shape = single_concat`. The brief specifies a single linear theatrical-style teaser, landscape, no narrator, ending on a title hit, and never asks for chapters, scoreboard widgets, or persistent overlays. Rewarding the absence of persistent overlays tests the shape contract without penalising brief decorative elements. Burned-in English subtitles on dialogue do not count as an overlay for this item.
items.check: Inspect the recap end-to-end. Identify any persistent overlay element other than burned-in dialogue subtitles or the closing title card. Compute the fraction of total recap runtime over which any such overlay is visible. Pass if that visible-fraction does not exceed 50%. Judge cites the timestamp range during which any candidate overlay appears and names the type of overlay (scoreboard / lower-third / chapter card / attribution panel / other) if present.

items.criterion: A first-time viewer can identify, from the recap's visuals alone (no English voiceover required), that the protagonist is pursuing violent retribution against a specific antagonist character, i.e. the recap establishes the protagonist as the agent of a directed revenge, not as a passive victim or a generic action protagonist.
items.why: This is the teaser's core promise. Confinement (V-IMPRISONMENT) and release (V-RELEASE) are tested separately; this item tests only the violent-pursuit-of-a-specific-target axis.
items.check: Judge writes a one-sentence vengeance-premise summary derived only from the recap (form: "The protagonist [does X] toward [specific antagonist character] because [implied motive or no motive]") and cites the recap timestamp(s) that ground the directed-retribution reading. Pass if the sentence contains both a directed action by the protagonist AND a specific antagonist character referenced in the recap.

items.criterion: If any adult young woman appears in the recap, every shot of her depicts her in an adult-ally or ambiguous-stranger framing only, interacting with the protagonist as a peer, a stranger, or an indeterminate acquaintance, and never in a framing that suggests parent/child relationship (no on-screen text labeling, no juxtaposition with a child or family photo, no intercut with childhood imagery).
items.why: The source repeatedly intercuts the female lead with family-photo collages and childhood footage (twist-revealing). The teaser must keep her relationship ambiguous.
items.check: For each recap timestamp at which an adult young woman appears, verify the shot is not adjacent (within ±2 seconds) to any family-photo composition, any child's face, any photo-album visual, or any on-screen text indicating "daughter" / "father" / "family". Pass if every shot of her clears this. Judge cites every female-character recap timestamp and the adjacent ±2 s context.

items.criterion: The recap contains at least one shot of the protagonist walking alone (no companion in frame) through a city street, daylight or dusk, framed as descent / re-entry into the world.
items.why: Source calibration: the "can I return to being Oh Dae-su" lone-walk at 04:15–04:18 captures the post-release re-entry beat; the golden uses an equivalent suit + sunglasses street walk.
items.check: Judge cites a recap timestamp showing the protagonist alone in a city street, walking, no companion visible.

items.criterion: The recap does not contain any snow / white-out / "THE END" red wood-block title / hypnosis-session / final-smile-or-frown imagery.
items.why: Curator-named spoiler boundary: the post-revenge resolution must not appear. The source surfaces it at 02:05–02:07 and 05:10–05:22. This item handles the soft case; large-magnitude penalty N-CRIT-POST-REVENGE handles the catastrophic case.
items.check: Inspect the recap end-to-end. Pass if no frame shows: a snowfield with bare trees; the words "THE END" in red wood-block typography on snow; a clinical hypnosis-couch / hand-on-forehead session; or the final ambiguous smile-into-frown close-up. Judge cites the offending timestamp if found.

items.criterion: The recap does not contain any composite/triptych/split-screen frame that juxtaposes a family-portrait still photograph with a young woman's face and the protagonist's reaction-face, nor any photograph or photo album presented as evidence of family relationship.
items.why: Curator-named spoiler boundary: the incest-reveal twist is surfaced in the source at 01:34–01:37 (family-photo + Mi-do + Dae-su collage), 02:13–02:16 (photo albums), and 04:54–04:57 (sexual-encounter photo set). This item is the high-frequency soft case for the same axis as critical N-CRIT-INCEST-REVEAL.
items.check: Inspect the recap end-to-end for any composite frame (two or more sub-frames within one frame) involving any of: a small framed family-style photograph, a young woman's face, a man's reaction shot. Pass if no such composite appears. Judge cites the offending timestamp if found.

items.criterion: The recap does not contain any shot of the antagonist (well-dressed adult male) inside an elevator with a firearm or in the act of self-harm, nor any shot of his collapse / death.
items.why: Source surfaces this at 02:01–02:04 and 04:49–04:51. Showing it forecloses the antagonist arc and is a post-revenge spoiler.
items.check: Inspect the recap for any shot of the V-ANTAGONIST character inside an elevator interior, holding a gun, or in a collapse / death pose. Pass if none. Judge cites the offending timestamp if found.

items.criterion: The recap does not contain any shot of a person cutting their own tongue, holding scissors near or inside their mouth with visible blood, or holding a severed body part.
items.why: Source surfaces tongue-cutting at 01:54–01:56, 04:13–04:15, 04:34–04:39. This is a late-stage spoiler beat.
items.check: Inspect the recap for any frame containing scissors at a mouth, blood streaming from the mouth in a clinical / self-harm context, or a held severed appendage. Pass if none. Judge cites the offending timestamp if found.

items.criterion: The recap does not contain any reproduction of a classical / Renaissance / neoclassical oil painting depicting a nude or partially-nude Greek figure, a sphinx, or an Oedipus-and-Sphinx composition, nor any side-by-side comparison frame placing a film still next to such a painting.
items.why: The source uses the Oedipus painting at 04:13–04:22 to thematically deliver the twist. Including it leaks the twist by reference and also breaks tone (essay-analytical material).
items.check: Inspect the recap for any frame containing a classical-painting reproduction with a nude figure, a sphinx, or text labeling "Oedipus". Also fail if a side-by-side comparison frame appears. Pass if none. Judge cites the offending timestamp if found.

items.criterion: At least one continuous Korean-language spoken line (≥ 1.0 seconds of spoken Korean) is audible in the recap.
items.why: Curator-named requirement: preserve subtitled-Korean dialogue continuity. The source has Korean dialogue under embedded clips (e.g. "Think hard." at the sushi bar, "Let go!" at the police station).
items.check: Listen to the recap audio end-to-end. Pass if at least one continuous Korean-language utterance ≥ 1.0 s is audible. The utterance must be in Korean, not dubbed English. Judge cites the recap timestamp of the utterance.

items.criterion: For every spoken line in the recap (any language, including any Korean dialogue), legible English subtitle or caption text is visible within the safe area of the frame (not cropped off the top, bottom, or sides) for the duration of that line.
items.why: Curator-named requirement: subtitled-Korean dialogue continuity. The brief tells the editor "the burned-in English subtitles plainly readable on every line that's spoken." The source has burned-in English captions on every embedded film clip; cropping, zooming, or rendering on top of the captions destroys them. Required by diversity constraint `audio_policy = source_with_burned_captions`.
items.check: Identify every audible spoken line in the recap. For each, verify legible English caption text is visible inside the frame boundary while that line is being spoken. Pass if every spoken line is covered. Judge cites at least two recap timestamps where a spoken line carries a legible visible caption, plus the timestamp of any spoken line missing a caption if found.

items.criterion: A music bed (instrumental score, ambient pad, or rhythmic underscore) is audible for at least 75% of the recap's runtime.
items.why: Trailer convention; the golden is carried by a melancholic piano-led orchestral score. A bare-dialogue or full-silence recap fails the teaser register.
items.check: Listen to the recap end-to-end and estimate the fraction of runtime over which any musical instrument or sustained pad is audible. Pass if ≥ 75%. Judge cites at least two recap timestamps within the music bed.

items.criterion: In a window of ±1.5 seconds around the first appearance of the "OLDBOY" title card, the music bed either drops to silence or to a sustained low drone that does not include a rhythmic beat or melodic motion.
items.why: Trailer convention; the golden goes to silence at 01:46 just before the title hit. Reinforces "the title is the payoff".
items.check: Find the timestamp at which the title text first appears in the recap. Inspect the audio in [t−1.5 s, t+1.5 s]. Pass if the audio in that window is either silent or a sustained low drone with no audible beat or melodic line. Judge cites the title timestamp.

items.criterion: No English-language voiceover narration explaining plot, characters, or themes is audible at any point in the recap. This includes any audible call-to-action phrase ("subscribe", "click below", "for Earthling Cinema", "click the subscribe button", "follow", "like and subscribe") and any English speech carrying comedic vocal affect (laugh-tracked sting, exaggerated word delivery, joke punchline cadence).
items.why: The source has a dense English essay narration; carrying any of it into the recap turns the teaser into an explainer. Brief explicitly forbids English narration. Catastrophic case (recognizable host lines) covered by penalty S-CRIT-HOST-AUDIO. Unified check covers general lecture, subscribe-pitch, and comedic-register host-audio bleed.
items.check: Listen to the recap end-to-end. Pass if no English voiceover narrator is audible AND no CTA phrase is audible AND any English speech present (if any) is delivered in a flat / serious / non-comedic register. (English subtitle text on-screen is allowed; spoken English narration is not.) Brief on-screen English text such as critic quotes and the title card is allowed if not spoken. Judge cites the recap timestamp of any offending English narration line.

items.criterion: The recap audio contains no abrupt cut that truncates a spoken syllable mid-word.
items.why: Sloppy concatenation produces clipped audio; trailer polish forbids this.
items.check: Listen to the recap end-to-end. Pass if no spoken syllable is truncated by a hard cut. Judge cites the offending recap timestamp if found.

items.criterion: The recap audio contains no continuous silence longer than 3.0 seconds outside the silence-at-title window allowed by S-SILENCE-AT-TITLE.
items.why: Long unintended silences read as missing audio; trailer polish forbids this.
items.check: Listen to the recap end-to-end. Identify any continuous silence segment longer than 3.0 s and check it does not fall within ±1.5 s of the OLDBOY title appearance. Pass if no such off-title silence exists. Judge cites the offending recap timestamp if found.

items.criterion: One or more frames in the recap show a pale-skinned adult male character with stylized handlebar-mustache eyebrows (eyebrows curled outward like a moustache) in a dark high-collared minimalist shirt, standing or framed against a red velvet curtain and/or beside a glass dome on a plinth.
items.why: Source calibration: this is the Earthling Cinema host ("Garyx Wormuloid"). He occupies roughly half the source runtime (≈34 windows between 00:08 and 05:51) and is the strongest source-contamination signal. Any frame in the recap is catastrophic.
items.check: Inspect the recap end-to-end for any frame matching the described visual: handlebar-mustache eyebrows + dark high-collared shirt + red curtain backdrop or glass-dome plinth. Pass=true (deduction fires) if at least one such frame appears. Judge cites the offending recap timestamp.

items.criterion: At least one recognizable English narration line spoken by the source host is audible in the recap, including but not limited to: "Earthling Cinema", "I am your host", "Garyx Wormuloid", "Old Boy tells the story of", "Wu Jin", "Mido", "for Earthling Cinema", "click the subscribe button", or any line that recounts the film's plot in first-person-essayist register.
items.why: Source calibration: the host narrates ≈90% of the source audio in a recognizable comedic-essay register. Carrying his audio into the teaser collapses the deliverable into an explainer.
items.check: Listen to the recap end-to-end. Pass=true (deduction fires) if any English narration line clearly from the same essay register is audible. Use the listed line cues as positive markers; broader essay-cadence English narration also fires. Judge cites the offending recap timestamp and transcribes the offending phrase.

items.criterion: The recap contains any visual that, on its own, makes legible the twist that the female lead is a blood relative of the protagonist. Triggering visuals include: a composite frame juxtaposing a family-style group portrait (man, woman, young child) with a separate close-up of the adult female lead and/or the protagonist's horrified reaction face; any on-screen text identifying the female lead as "daughter" or naming a parent-child relationship; a still photo set of intimate adult contact between the protagonist and the female lead intercut with childhood imagery; or a side-by-side comparison frame placing the protagonist or the female lead next to a classical Oedipus painting in a framing that implies identity.
items.why: Curator-named primary spoiler. The source surfaces this at 01:34–01:37 (family-photo + Mi-do + Dae-su triptych), 01:41–01:43 (daughter-growing-up surveillance footage), 02:13–02:16 (photo album), 04:13–04:22 (Oedipus painting comparison), and 04:54–04:57 (sexual-encounter photo stills). Maximum severity: -60.
items.check: Inspect the recap end-to-end. Pass=true (deduction fires) if any of the triggering visual patterns above is present. Judge cites the offending recap timestamp and describes which trigger fired.

items.criterion: The recap contains a snowfield exterior with bare trees, OR the words "THE END" rendered in red wood-block typography on snow, OR a clinical hypnosis-session shot with a hand placed on a seated subject's forehead, OR the protagonist's final ambiguous close-up that begins as a smile and falls to a frown.
items.why: Curator-named secondary spoiler: the post-revenge resolution. Source surfaces at 02:05–02:07 and 05:10–05:22. Including any of these forecloses the teaser's mystery.
items.check: Inspect the recap end-to-end. Pass=true (deduction fires) if any of the listed visuals appears. Judge cites the offending recap timestamp.

items.criterion: At least one spoken line (in any language, Korean, English, or otherwise) plays in the recap for ≥ 1.0 s without legible English subtitle/caption text visible within the safe area of the frame during that line.
items.why: Curator-named requirement: a Korean-source trailer with no subtitles or burned-in translation fails the deliverable. Required magnitude for diversity constraint `audio_policy = source_with_burned_captions`. The soft presence of S-CAPTIONS-EVERY-LINE is replaced with catastrophic failure when any spoken line plays without an accompanying readable caption. Source-Korean lines are the dominant trigger (e.g. "Think hard.", "Let go!"), but the criterion also fires on any added non-Korean speech that ships without captions.
items.check: Listen to the recap audio for any continuous spoken-line utterance of ≥ 1.0 s in any language. For each such utterance, inspect the recap video during the utterance for readable English caption text within the safe area of the frame (not cropped off any side). Pass=true (deduction fires) if at least one such ≥ 1.0 s utterance has zero legible English caption text in-frame. Judge cites the offending utterance timestamp and transcribes the spoken line.
